newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - July 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - July 16.

text.p: These are some leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO -- The Hong Kong government announced a massive land sale programme aimed at providing 146,000 residential units over the next five years and curbing property prices.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- A survey showed the moral standards of Hong Kong's young people were falling. More than half of those surveyed said they could tolerate corruption in the commercial sector. Twenty percent said they were willing to resort to bribery to solve problems and most agreed that bribery was the quickest way to get things done.

-- APPLE DAILY -- Official figures show about 100,000 children of Hong Kong parents live in China's southern province of Guangdong. According to the present quota system, it would take at least six years for them to resettle in Hong Kong. The Immigration Department is trying to persuade Beijing to increase the daily immigration quota for children from 66 to 90.

-- A major gang boss in the Portuguese-run enclave of Macau has successfully passed the background checks for emigration to Canada through investment. He was planning to buy an apartment in the exclusive Fraserview area of Vancouver.
-- WEN WEI PO -- A total of 3.6 billion yuan was invested in the China's Three Gorges hydroelectric dam project in the first half of the year.

-- TIN TIN DAILY -- Doctors in the southern Chinese city of Guangzhou removed a huge object from the stomach of a young man, which was made up of human hair. The patient had a habit of eating hair, because he found it tasty, especially when he got depressed.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- A closure order imposed on a local company, Rex International Development Co, which was accused of helping Iran produce "weapons of mass destruction", was lifted by government security bosses on condition the firm shut down voluntarily.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Property and infrastructure company Hopewell Holdigs said it was selling its remaining 19.99 percent stake in Consolidated Electric Power Asia to U.S.-based Southern Co, despite a string of earlier denials.
